# terminal_styles

> Small Ada library crate for ANSI terminal text decoration helpers.

terminal_styles provides one public package, `Terminal_Styles`, with helpers for semantic
status-line formatting and explicit ANSI SGR styling. It is intended for CLI
programs that need consistent colorized output while respecting `NO_COLOR` and
TTY-aware color behavior.

## Primary Files

- `README.md`: user documentation, dependency instructions, API summary, build/test commands
- `src/terminal_styles.ads`: public API specification
- `src/terminal_styles.adb`: implementation
- `tests/`: AUnit test crate
- `examples/basic/`: minimal consumer example crate
- `LICENSE`: MIT OR Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception
- `alire.toml`: Alire package metadata

## Public API

Package: `Terminal_Styles`

Types:

- `Style_Role`: `Role_Info`, `Role_Success`, `Role_Error`, `Role_Warning`, `Role_Muted`, `Role_Header`
- `Text_Decoration`: ANSI text decorations such as bold, italic, underline, reverse, conceal, crossed out, framed, encircled, overlined, and reset/disable variants
- `Terminal_Color`: default, standard 8 ANSI colors, and bright 8 ANSI colors
- `Color_Policy`: `Color_Auto`, `Color_Always`, `Color_Never`

Operations:

- `Set_Color_Policy`: set the process-wide color policy
- `Current_Color_Policy`: read the process-wide color policy
- `Color_Enabled`: report whether ANSI styling should currently be emitted
- `Decorate`: wrap text with ANSI SGR sequences by role, decoration, colors, or decoration plus colors
- `Marker`: return an ASCII marker for a semantic role
- `Line`: return a role marker plus decorated text

## Behavior Notes

- Default color policy is `Color_Auto`.
- `Color_Auto` emits ANSI styling only when stdout is a TTY and `NO_COLOR` is not set.
- `Color_Always` emits ANSI styling regardless of `NO_COLOR` and TTY detection.
- `Color_Never` suppresses ANSI styling.
- `Set_Color_Policy` changes process-wide library state; tests or callers that force it should restore the prior value.
- `Line` keeps ASCII markers even when ANSI styling is disabled.

## Ada Usage

```ada
with Ada.Text_IO;
with Terminal_Styles;

procedure Demo is
begin
   Ada.Text_IO.Put_Line (Terminal_Styles.Line ("ready", Terminal_Styles.Role_Success));
   Ada.Text_IO.Put_Line
     (Terminal_Styles.Decorate
        ("warning",
         Terminal_Styles.Decoration_Bold,
         Terminal_Styles.Color_Yellow));
end Demo;
```

## Build And Test

Toolchain rule: every active manifest pins `gnat_native = "=15.2.1"`. Do not
run plain system GNAT/GPR tools; use `alr exec -- ...` and require
`alr exec -- gnatls --version` to report `GNATLS 15.x`.

```sh
alr exec -- gnatls --version
alr build
cd tests
alr build
./bin/tests
```

Example crate:

```sh
cd examples/basic
alr build
./bin/terminal_styles_basic_example
```

## Scope

terminal_styles does not handle terminal capability databases, Windows console mode
setup, cursor movement, layouts, prompts, progress bars, or rich terminal UI.
It only formats strings with ANSI SGR codes and role markers.
